The key insight is: the hidden verifier:
1. Starts from a pristine checkout of the repository at the start state
2. Applies my changes as a patch
3. Restores test files, conftest.py, sitecustomize, .pth files and packaging config
4. Writes the release's own test files over it
5. Runs the release's new tests (grouped per requirement) and every pre-existing test with pytest

So my changes will be applied as a patch to the original code, then the hidden tests will be written. My goal is to make those hidden tests pass.

But it says "the hidden verifier... writes the release's own test files over it" - so the tests are written by the verifier, not by me. So the tests are predetermined and my changes to the code must make them pass.
